rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3 - own UAV survey (Parrot Anafi, 24 May 2019) of a 0.78 ha maize field at Legnaro, NE Italy, with own classification and prescription-map outputs. Q2: Section 3 and Table 2 - area to be sprayed computed from UAV-derived prescription maps ranges from 2.18% to 18.92% of the field (MLC 14.59-2.18%, ANN 18.92-3.75%, OBIA 15.82-3.49%/5.48%) versus full-field blanket spraying. Q7: Section 2.4 and Discussion - grid sizes were set according to sprayer capability (single-nozzle vs boom-section control); authors state the effectiveness of the maps is tied to matching detection scale with the available spraying technology and that maps require equipment capable of section or nozzle-level control, noting such sprayers are not yet widely adopted in Italy. Q8: Discussion - authors state no spraying was carried out, the maps were not validated in field trials, cost-effectiveness studies are missing, results from a single maize field, and there is a trade-off between herbicide savings and risk of under-treatment.
rows.notes: The passage misreads the study in several ways: (1) the crop was maize, not vegetable crops; (2) the figures 2.18-18.92% are the remaining area to be sprayed as a share of the field (i.e., reductions of roughly 81-98%), not the reduction itself; (3) the study does not say ANN was more efficient - it reports ANN had higher sensitivity and produced larger treated areas, with MLC more conservative, and explicitly declines to compare algorithms. Classification accuracy (Table 1) is taken from Mattivi et al. 2021, not the present study. No herbicide was actually applied and no weed-control outcome was measured; the result is a GIS-computed treated-area reduction from one field, one date, one crop. Q7 is a cautious yes since the dependence on sprayer precision is stated as a practical requirement rather than merely an observed gradient. No dispersion or uncertainty measures reported.

notes: Full text available and complete. Single-field, single-date case study generating prescription-map scenarios; results are planned treated areas, not realised herbicide savings or weed control.
